_what: Where a look applies, as DATA. The person's account wears one look (input `current-screen-look`); that is the last rule, everywhere else, and changing it in one place changes every screen. On top of it a person keeps an ordered list of look rules in the workspace record `record_key`: each { id, label?, when, look_id, time_zone?, on?, by?, made_at? }, where `when` is the formula engine's rule tree (parts/formula-engine/rules) over the facts below (null: always) and `look_id` is the look worn where it holds. The first rule that holds wins; when none does the account's look is worn. `facts` are what a rule can name: `host` is the app or place the screen is drawn in (`hosts`, found by `detect`: a page global, a user agent pattern, the page's protocol; the first row that matches, `web` last), `device` the kind of device (`devices`, by user agent), `device_id` and `place` (the screen or area of the app, such as get-started) are said by whoever draws the screen, `hour` (0-23) and `weekday` are read from the time in the rule's own `time_zone` (the device's own zone when the rule has none), and `now` is the moment itself. A new app, device kind or fact is a row here; nothing in code names one. A look the person no longer has lets the next rule, and then the account's look, through.

default_rule.words: The look you wear on every screen that no rule above picks.
